text: Today, Seabrook Town played against Harbour City in the Northbridge League. Harbour City started strong and scored two goals first! Elias Okafor scored right before halftime with a clever pass from Marek Barros, who was the best player on the field [#905] [#975]. But Seabrook Town didn’t give up. They pressed hard and attacked quickly, scoring four goals in the second half! The coolest moment was when Kian Romano scored two incredible goals in the last minutes to win the game 4-2 [#1882] [#1906]. Seabrook’s fast, wide players helped them take the ball and score many times [#1448]. It was a thrilling match full of teamwork and late surprises. Seabrook Town showed how exciting football can be with smart moves and never giving up!

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for kid audience in en

- Kian Romano scored twice in stoppage time with xG of 0.605 and 0.952, turning the match in favor of Seabrook Town [#1882, #1906]  
- Marek Barros, player of the match, scored and assisted two goals with a rating of 9.8 and covered 14.37 km [#975]  
- Seabrook Town dominated overall with 22 shots, 9 on target, and xG of 3.44 vs. Harbour City's 10 shots, 5 on target, and xG of 1.03  
- Harbour City received a red card for Joon Whitfield at 43', reducing their defensive strength before conceding goals [#870]  
- Seabrook Town increased pressing and directness at 65', aiding in their comeback from 0-2 to 4-2 victory [#1361]

- Seabrook Town, playing in a 3-4-3 formation with a wide, crossing style, relied heavily on regains and quick transitions to create opportunities, as seen in their first-half big chance at 35' where Tariq Marlowe had a rapid regaining-based shot off target [697,698]. This reflects a pressing and quick counter-attacking aspect within their wide setup.

- Harbour City, in a 4-2-3-1 formation favoring patient short passing, demonstrated controlled build-up play for their first goal at 45', involving 17 passes over nearly a minute before Elias Okafor scored from a through ball by Marek Barros [904,905]. This illustrates their style of methodical possession and breaking down defenses via sustained passing sequences.

- The tactical change by Seabrook Town at 65'—pressing higher, playing more direct, and raising their defensive line height—was aimed at chasing the game after trailing 2-1, leading to increased pressing intensity (ppda 0.84 → 0.66), more direct attacks, and line height (0.72 from 0.6), thereby facilitating goals from turnovers and quicker counters, such as Callum Varga’s goal at 69' following a regain and short passing combination [1361,1447,1448].

- Late in the match, Seabrook’s goals at 90+2' and 90+3' demonstrate exploitation of open-play counter-attacks and quick combinations after regains (notably Kian Romano’s chances created off regained balls), reflecting the success of their high pressing and directness tactics implemented to overturn the deficit and win 4-2 [1881,1882,1905,1906].

- Harbour City’s low pressing intensity and patient buildup contrasted with Seabrook Town’s rising directness and pressing, resulting in fewer box touches (Harbour 41 total, with only 12 second half) and a drop in field tilt in the second half (to 36.7%), which indicates they were increasingly pushed back by Seabrook’s wide and crossing style as the game progressed.
